title: North Ostrobothnia: 2.5 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €98,500 a year
markdown:
# North Ostrobothnia: 2.5 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €98,500 a year

> Closes 2.5 of 7.1 missing patients a year (35%) · €98,500 of €1M · €901,500 left: nothing more pays off on today's evidence

## The gap

Of 100 lung cancer patients in North Ostrobothnia, 24 get treatment that aims to cure. In Finland it is 27. That is about 7 patients a year. [^care_curative] Against the best quarter of counties, 14.2 patients a year are missing (range 8.5–19.4). [^model] Against Finland as a whole: 0.0 fewer operated, 7.1 fewer given radiotherapy that aims to cure. [^model] In the OYS collaborative area, waits from diagnosis to treatment are not longer: 31.2 days, Finland 36.9. [^care_time_to_treatment] Fewer are treated to cure. [^care_curative] The share is also below the 29.7% that residents' age would predict. [^model]

## The target

Raise the share of lung cancer patients treated to cure from 23.6% to 24.8% by 2028: 2.5 more patients a year (range 0.0–5.0), for €98,500 a year, about €39,718 per extra patient. [^care_curative][^model] That closes 35% of the measured shortfall against Finland as a whole (7.1 patients a year). [^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | More patients treated to cure a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated**[^ev_sbrt_pathway_1]. Chief physician of oncology; chief of radiotherapy at the university hospital | €44,000 | 1.7 (0.0–3.4) | Write the referral rule: every stage I patient not accepted for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy the same week. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 23.6% → 24.4% by 2028 |
| 2 | **Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment**[^ev_prehab_fitness_assessment_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; leads of rehabilitation and geriatrics | €54,500 | 0.8 (0.0–1.7) | Decide that no stage I-III patient is recorded as "not fit" without an exercise test, and book the physiotherapy group. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 23.6% → 24.0% by 2028 |
| | **Total** | **€98,500** | **2.5 (0.0–5.0)** | | |

No trial has measured these effects; the low end of every range is zero. The ranges do not add up to the range of the total, because the measures share one ceiling. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €1,273,817 a year; modelled to avoid 2.2 deaths a year (0.5–5.8). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of patients treated to cure: 23.6% (2019–2023, measured) → 24.8% by 2028. [^care_curative][^model]
- The registry's public figures cover 2019–2023; count these each month from the county's own records. [^care_curative]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

In the model, the remaining €901,500 buys nothing more, because the reachable part of the measured shortfall limits these measures, not money. [^model] More could come from low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision. [^model] Ranking measures by deaths avoided would also show other uses. [^model] Lung cancer causes about 165 deaths a year in North Ostrobothnia, and this plan is modelled to avoid 0.4 of them a year (0.0–1.5). [^deaths] [^model]

## Pilot ask

Pilot: North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county, 6 months: (1) stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated, (2) fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. KPI: share of patients treated to cure 23.6% → 24.8% by 2028. [^model]

## Limits

- Effects are ranges, not probabilities: the lowest and highest results when every assumed effect moves together from low to high. [^model]
- The expected share is adjusted only for residents' age, not stage, fitness, histology, smoking or recording completeness. County figures cannot show cause. [^model]
- The symptom-to-treatment clock is estimated, not measured: a check against 3 measured outcomes found that 0 of them match it in the expected direction beyond what chance allows. [^model]
